ledger.x: -31: Satakarni I's conquest of Western Malwa (Ujjain).
28 BCE: the Satavahanas end the Kanva dynasty.
early 2nd century CE: Gautamiputra Satakarni takes South Kosala.

c. 124 CE: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeats Nahapana. Most historians now agree (Gautamiputra page) that Gautamiputra and Nahapana were contemporaries and that Gautamiputra defeated Nahapana; Dhavalikar dates it c. 124 CE (his 18th regnal year), Fynes after 71 CE, Bhandare 78 CE. His Nashik inscription calls him 'king…

c. 127 CE: Kshatrapa Rudradaman takes back Nahapana's former lands. 'It is possible that by the end of his reign, Gautamiputra lost some of his territory to the Kardamakas'; Rudradaman 'regained all the former territories previously held by Nahapana' except 'the southern territory of Poona and Nasik' (Rudradaman page…

c. 154 CE: Aparanta returns to the Satavahanas. Rudradaman 'conceded the country of Aparanta to Vashishtiputra Satakarni' as dowry (Rudradaman page, undated; the daughter's marriage ended the hostilities). 154 is Cliopatria's year; the page gives none. Vashishtiputra Satakarni's own page dates his reign 158-165 CE…

c. 184 CE: Yajna Sri Satakarni recovers the south of the Western Satraps' lands. He 'defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions in western and central India' and 'not only ruled Aparanta, but probably also the eastern part of the Central Provinces' (Majumdar). The page gives only reign…

c. 203 CE: the Abhiras take the north around Nashik. 'The Abhiras captured the northern parts of the kingdom' in Yajna Satakarni's last years (Satavahana page, no year). 203 is the end of the longest reign variant (174-203) and matches 'Established: 203' in the Abhira dynasty infobox (Abhira page, read 2026-10-19)…

c. 224 CE: the Satavahana empire fragments. 'After the death of Pulumavi IV, the Satavahana empire fragmented into five smaller kingdoms': a collateral branch in the north, the Abhiras around Nashik, the Andhra Ikshvakus in the Krishna-Guntur region, the Chutus of Banavasi in northern Karnataka and the Pallavas in the…

wars.name: Kharavela's expedition against Satakarni
wars.outcome: Inconclusive in the sources: in his year 2 Kharavela 'dispatched a large army ... towards the western regions' against Satakarni, reaching 'the banks of the Krishnabena river'; scholars read it as a threat, a tribute arrangement or a friendly act.

wars.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni's war on the Kshaharatas
wars.outcome: Satavahana victory: Nahapana's 'Khakharata' family 'rooted out' (Nashik inscription) and his coins restruck at Jogalthembi.

wars.name: Rudradaman's wars with Satakarni
wars.outcome: Rudradaman 'twice in fair fight completely defeated Satakarni' (the Junagadh inscription, dated 150 CE) but spared him through their marriage tie; he regained Nahapana's former lands; Aparanta passed back as dowry.

wars.name: Yajna Sri Satakarni's recovery from the Western Satraps
wars.outcome: Yajna 'defeated the Western Satraps and reconquered their southern regions in western and central India'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is dated; the pages name provinces (aharas such as Govardhana) and inscription findspots, not lines.
